chapter_title: Chương 196: Phỏng vấn Tuần san Internet

segments.title: Chương 196: Phỏng vấn Tuần san Internet
segments.content:
Chapter 199: 0196 Interview with *Internet Weekly*

There are many ginkgo trees on the Peking University campus. Once autumn arrives, the ground is covered in gold.

Chen Guiliang rode his bicycle, passing through the alternating light and shadow of the trees, occasionally ringing his battered bell to remind pedestrians to make way.

Li Yong, a reporter from *Internet Weekly*, was waiting just inside the south gate of Peking University.

When he saw someone ride over and stop, he was clearly taken aback for a moment. "Are you President Chen?"

"You must be Reporter Li?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Yong nodded. "Yes."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Should we find a coffee shop, or pick a scenic spot on campus?"

"Either is fine. I'll defer to my host," Li Yong said with a smile.

"Hop on," Chen Guiliang said, patting the back seat.

Li Yong swung his leg over the bicycle. "I haven't ridden on the back of a bike in years. I never thought the next time I did, it would be President Chen's."

"Then I'm quite honored," Chen Guiliang laughed, pedaling a few hundred meters with the reporter before turning into a corner of Yannan Garden.

The vegetation here was lush, serene, and quiet, with old buildings from the late Qing and Republican eras nearby.

"Meow."

An old cat basking on a flowerbed opened its eyes at the sound, then lazily meowed at the humans with its eyes half-closed.

*Internet Weekly* was an authoritative magazine under the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and it was also hosting its annual internet gala next month.

Since they had requested an interview, Chen Guiliang had to give them face.

Li Yong took out an invitation card. "It's on the 1st of next month. It's the second China Internet Development Forum and the 2005 Top 100 Chinese Commercial Websites award ceremony. An electronic invitation has already been emailed to your company, but since I was coming to interview you, President Chen, I thought I'd bring the physical copy as well."

"Thank you for your trouble, Reporter Li." Chen Guiliang accepted the invitation card.

Li Yong smiled. "The list for the Top 100 Chinese Commercial Websites has already been finalized. Aren't you going to ask if your website made the list, President Chen?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Just being able to attend the gala is enough for me, but of course, I'd be even happier to be in the top 100. Is it Xiaonei Wang?"

"That's right," Li Yong nodded.

Xiaonei Wang's user base was growing larger and larger, and its operating costs were skyrocketing.

For the month of October, the server, bandwidth, and hosting fees for Xiaonei Wang alone had soared to 1.7 million yuan, and that wasn't even counting other costs.

On top of that, Kaixin Wang's user base was also surging, causing ByteDance's operating costs to rise sharply. The venture capital funds the company had secured could last for six more months at most.

*Quan Yu Tianxia* was in its growth and expansion phase and wouldn't be able to provide much in shareholder dividends this year.

ByteDance had to tough it out.

After sharing the good news, Li Yong added a reminder, "For the '2005 Chinese New Economy Figure of the Year' award to be presented early next year, Professor He from your university has recommended you as one of the candidates. Online voting is currently underway. Your vote count, President Chen, is temporarily ranked 87th. You could do a little promoting to rally some votes."

Professor He was a professor at Peking University's Guanghua School of Management and a judge for this year's "New Economy Figure of the Year" award, allowed to recommend three candidates.

Chen Guiliang had taken his class as a freshman.

The so-called "New Economy Figures" were, naturally, distinguished from traditional entrepreneurs.

To be honest, very few netizens would go out of their way to vote.

Moreover, netizens had never heard of more than 90% of the candidates. They hadn't even heard of their companies' names.

If Chen Guiliang casually wrote an article on his Xiaonei Wang and Kaixin Wang accounts to drum up support, his vote count could probably enter the top ten.

The organizers had naturally anticipated such a situation, so public voting only accounted for 40% of the weight. Even if you were in the top five in online votes, you could still be eliminated in the end.

Li Yong chatted casually with Chen Guiliang for a few moments before taking out a small notebook and a recording pen to begin the interview. "I'd like to ask about a few different topics this time. The first is Kaixin Market."

"Oh?" Chen Guiliang was slightly surprised.

Li Yong said, "According to statistics from relevant departments, the market size of classified advertising in China is currently between 10 and 30 billion yuan. It is projected to potentially exceed 50 billion yuan in three years. Kaixin Market's data is growing rapidly. What made you decide to enter this field?"

Chen Guiliang was highly skeptical of the accuracy of this data.

"Since Xiaonei Wang and Kaixin Wang are providing online community services, buying and selling transactions are a part of that," Chen Guiliang said.

Li Yong asked, "Some of your industry peers are very dissatisfied with Kaixin Market's free model. Do you think the free model is sustainable in the long run?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It's doing alright. Kaixin Market already turned a profit last month."

Well, a profit of over 3,000 yuan was still a profit.

At this time, there were hundreds, if not thousands, of classified advertising websites in China. And most of them were regional websites, focusing on the market of one or several provinces.

Currently, the largest was Koubei Wang, founded by a veteran employee who had left Alibaba.

The second largest was Bigou Wang, whose founder had previously been in the blogging business; his blog had already been acquired by BlogCN.

When Chen Guiliang entered this track, portal websites like Sina, NetEase, and Sohu had also rushed in.

But only Chen Guiliang, relying on Xiaonei Wang and Kaixin Wang, persisted with the "free model."

Li Yong said, "The progenitor of classified advertising websites is Craigslist in the United States. It seems that in all of China, only Kaixin Market is following Craigslist's path, while other websites have adapted to local conditions. Aren't you worried it won't acclimate well?"

"Kaixin Market turned a profit last month," Chen Guiliang stated a fact.

Li Yong asked, "How much was the profit?"

"That's a business secret." Chen Guiliang certainly wouldn't say it was only just over 3,000 yuan.

From its creation until now, Kaixin Market had already cost several hundred thousand yuan, and who knew when they would recoup the costs.

Li Yong asked a few more questions about classified advertising before turning to Weibo. "Whether it's Xiaonei Wang, Kaixin Wang, or Kaixin Market, they are all models that already exist in the United States. But a product like Weibo seems to be your original creation, President Chen?"

"Limited by technology, it's not very mature yet," Chen Guiliang said.

Li Yong said, "You're too modest, President Chen. Do you think the Weibo model can be widely adopted?"

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "We'll have to wait until 3G communication technology and high-performance mobile phones become more widespread. As things stand, the market's door has only just opened a crack."

Li Yong asked, "Do you think Weibo will be one of the directions for Web 2.0?"

"Yes," Chen Guiliang said.

Li Yong said, "An article in the American magazine *Time* last month said that industries like software, telecommunications, media, entertainment, and marketing will all be strongly impacted by Web 2.0 and will undergo earth-shattering changes. What are your thoughts on this?"

Chen Guiliang said, "I very much agree. If Weibo becomes big, it will be a disruption to the entertainment industry. More entertainment companies and celebrities will pay attention to this space. It could even change the traditional promotional methods of the entertainment industry."

After talking for a few more minutes, Li Yong said, "Some scholars are already starting to fantasize about Web 3.0. What are your thoughts on that?"

"Just wild speculation," Chen Guiliang said with a smile. "Web 2.0 isn't even mature yet. 3.0 is purely conjured from thin air."

"Do you know about online bookmarking services?" Li Yong asked.

Chen Guiliang nodded. "Xiaonei Wang and Kaixin Wang are about to launch an online bookmarking feature."

Online bookmarking was a new thing that had emerged last year, basically an online favorites folder with indexing capabilities. In Chen Guiliang's view, it was just a minor feature, yet a large number of online bookmarking companies had popped up.

Such companies would either be acquired by larger websites, evolve into online communities, or just have to run on passion until they went bankrupt. A business solely focused on online bookmarking was unlikely to attract venture capital.

But internet entrepreneurs always harbored illusions, believing anything was possible.

The interview lasted about 40 minutes. Li Yong shook hands with Chen Guiliang. He declined Chen Guiliang's offer of a ride on his bike, saying he wanted to walk around the Peking University campus and was waiting to interview Professor He of the Guanghua School of Management.

Chen Guiliang pushed his bicycle and left. Before he had even walked out of Yannan Garden, he saw his new roommate, Li Heng, under a tree.

"On a date?" Chen Guiliang asked casually.

Li Heng grinned. "Hehe."

"It's really a date," Chen Guiliang said. "Not bad, not bad, starting to date as a freshman."

Li Heng said, "It's not really dating. I posted an ad on Kaixin Market looking for love and included a link to my Xiaonei Wang homepage. I didn't expect a girl to actually respond. We've been chatting online for half a month. We arranged to meet here today."

"Good luck to you," Chen Guiliang said, patting his shoulder.

Students from Xiaonei Wang going to Kaixin Market to post ads seeking a relationship had recently seemed to become an alternative trend.

They could obviously post on Xiaonei Wang or a BBS, but they insisted on posting text ads on Kaixin Market, which didn't even have an image function.

Chen Guiliang rode his bike to the cafeteria to eat, then returned to the dorm for an afternoon nap.

Around noon, Li Heng returned to the dorm, looking dejected.

"What's wrong with you?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Li Heng sighed. "She's a sophomore, a senior. She's well-spoken, but... but she's just very plain-looking. Extremely plain. She's really enthusiastic toward me, and I don't quite know how to turn her down."

"Hahaha!" Chen Guiliang gloated.

This was an online relationship that had crashed and burned upon meeting in real life.

Li Heng said morosely, "Stop laughing."
